hints.title: Two-Variable Join Resolution
hints.text: Join Expressions twice with Variables: once for left_operand and once for right_operand.

hints.title: Conditional Operator Evaluation
hints.text: Use a conditional case expression inspecting operator against ">", "<", and "=".

hints.title: Output Literal Generation
hints.text: Return "true" when the condition holds and "false" otherwise.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT e.left_operand, e.operator, e.right_operand,
       CASE
           WHEN e.operator = '>' AND v1.value > v2.value THEN 'true'
           WHEN e.operator = '<' AND v1.value < v2.value THEN 'true'
           WHEN e.operator = '=' AND v1.value = v2.value THEN 'true'
           ELSE 'false'
       END AS value
FROM Expressions e
JOIN Variables v1 ON e.left_operand = v1.name
JOIN Variables v2 ON e.right_operand = v2.name;
```

complexity.notes: Joining variables via hash lookup and evaluating CASE condition executes in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated scalar subqueries for each operand require repetitive index lookups.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual joins resolve operand values in a single tabular scan.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Self-aliased joins mapping operands paired with exhaustive CASE evaluation.

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def eval_expression(variables: pd.DataFrame, expressions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    m1 = pd.merge(expressions, variables, left_on='left_operand', right_on='name', how='left')
    m2 = pd.merge(m1, variables, left_on='right_operand', right_on='name', how='left', suffixes=('_l', '_r'))
    def evaluate(row):
        op = row['operator']
        vl = row['value_l']
        vr = row['value_r']
        if op == '>' and vl > vr: return 'true'
        if op == '<' and vl < vr: return 'true'
        if op == '=' and vl == vr: return 'true'
        return 'false'
    m2['value'] = m2.apply(evaluate, axis=1)
    return m2[['left_operand', 'operator', 'right_operand', 'value']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Dual Merge and Rowwise Comparison
